or a handler's Content struct:
  [ ] /api/instances + :id launch|stop|disable|delete|unload|clean (InstanceHandler)
  [ ] personas CRUD (PersonaHandler)
  [ ] workflows CRUD + runs (WorkflowHandler, RunHandler)
  [ ] manual-workflows (ManualWorkflowHandler — validate/launch/get/delete, RAM-only)
  [ ] logs personas|workflows|sessions (LogHandler)
  [ ] knowledge files get|put|delete|list (KnowledgeHandler, ** catch-all)
  [ ] graph nodes + run logs (GraphHandler)

Served as text/plain by FileMiddleware — NO route is registered for it.
Touch ANY route under /api/instances/... → update this file in the same change.

# OpenLoop API

> OpenLoop automates AI-agent workflows. This is the machine-readable guide to
> the HTTP API behind the web UI at /. Base URL: http://localhost:54321
> Everything is scoped to an INSTANCE — the absolute path of the project folder
> the openloop worker runs in, URL-encoded.
> Example: /api/instances/%2Fhome%2Fme%2Fapp
> The list always includes one synthetic "global share" instance; address it
> the same way as any other.

## Quick start
1. GET /api/instances                    → find your instance `path`
2. GET /api/instances/:id/workflows      → see what it can run
3. POST /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows  { "workflow_id": "...", "ask": "..." }
4. GET /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/:runid  → poll until status != "running"

    curl -s localhost:54321/api/instances | jq '.instances[0].path'

## Conventions
- :id = encodeURIComponent(instanceFolderPath). Write bodies are JSON
  (Content-Type: application/json). List/get responses are JSON. Knowledge
  file bodies are raw text. Success: DELETE → 204, instance lifecycle → 200.
- Every route is under /api/instances/:id/... .

## Endpoints

Instances — list & lifecycle
  GET    /api/instances               → { instances:[{ path, parentPath?, state?,
                                  manualActive, manualCompleted, configEnabled?,
                                  processRunning?, isGlobalShare,
                                  graphMcpAuthMissing, dbSizeBytes, needsClean }] }
                                  state = { lastLoopAtUnixMs, activeRunningWorkflows,
                                            inactiveWorkflows }
                                  (configEnabled/processRunning are absent on the
                                  global-share instance.)
                                  graphMcpAuthMissing = count of graph nodes whose
                                  MCP was configured with a key this machine's
                                  secrets store doesn't hold (0 = nothing to say;
                                  the home page badges the instance cell, and
                                  /graph.html shows the same fact in its header
                                  and on the cells)
                                  dbSizeBytes = combined size of the instance's
                                  logs.db + logs.db-wal + logs.db-shm (0 = no db
                                  yet; the home page shows it as the DB pill);
                                  needsClean = dbSizeBytes >= the 1 GiB clean
                                  threshold — the server-owned verdict behind the
                                  Clean button
  POST   /api/instances/:id/launch    → start the worker for a folder   (200)
  POST   /api/instances/:id/stop      → kill the running process        (200)
  POST   /api/instances/:id/disable   → stop auto-loading on boot       (200)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/delete    → remove service registration     (200)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id           → unload                          (200)
  POST   /api/instances/:id/clean     → { dbSizeBytes, vacuumed, bytesReclaimed }
                                  Deletes every record/log older than 1 month
                                  (logs + their messages/parents, run_ends + their
                                  read markers, old graph run logs + markers),
                                  then VACUUMs. Old sessions lose follow-up
                                  ability (their run_ends row is gone — the
                                  follow-up gate 409s): intended, not a bug.
                                  A run started >1 mo ago that is still writing
                                  loses its log rows — accepted per contract.
                                  vacuumed=false = purge ok but the file couldn't
                                  compact while the instance was writing (partial
                                  clean; size settles on a later clean).

Personas — CRUD
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas        → { personas:[{ id, name, role, avatar? }] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid   → { name, role, about, task, avatar?, agent? }
  POST   /api/instances/:id/personas        body { id?, name?, role?, about?, task?,
                                                   avatar?, agent? }
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid   body: any subset (partial merge)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid   → 204

Workflows — CRUD
  GET    /api/instances/:id/workflows       → { workflows:[{ id, name, desc, ask }] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid  → { name, desc, every_secs, agent, ask, levels }
  POST   /api/instances/:id/workflows       body { id?, name?, desc?, every_secs?, agent?,
                                                   ask?, levels? }  (id ∈ [A-Za-z0-9_-])
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid  body: any subset (partial merge)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid  → 204
  GET    /api/instances/:id/workflows/:wid/runs  → { workflow_id, runs:[id] }

Manual runs — launch a workflow by hand, then watch it
  POST /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/validate  body { workflow_id, ask? }
                                              → { valid, errors[] }      (422 if invalid)
  POST /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows     body { workflow_id, ask? }
                                              → { id, workflow_id, ask, started_at,
                                                  status:"running", output }
  GET  /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows     → { workflows:[...] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/:runid  → status ∈ running|completed|failed
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/manual-workflows/:runid  → 204
  State is RAM-only (lost on restart); completed entries are swept ~1h later.
  `ask` is optional and defaults to the workflow's saved ask.

Logs — execution history (paginated: offset, count)
  GET /api/instances/:id/logs/personas?personaId=&offset=0&count=5
                                       → { logs[], stats:{ [pid]:{errors,success,total} },
                                           offset, count, total }
  GET /api/instances/:id/logs/workflows/:wid?offset=0&count=5
                                       → { logs[], offset, count, total }
  GET /api/instances/:id/logs/sessions/:session
                                       → { levels[], logs[] }  (full waterfall of one run)
  entry: { success, took, started_at(ms), ended_at(ms), id, workflowId, personaId?,
           agent, session?, level?, msg:{ input, output, parents:[{ id, text }] } }

Knowledge — per-persona plain-text file store
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge         → { files:[String] }
  GET    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge/**path  → raw text (text/plain)
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge/**path  body = raw text → 200
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/personas/:pid/knowledge/**path  → 204
  (** = catch-all sub-path. ../ traversal is rejected with 403.)

Graph — node graph per instance (powers /graph.html)
  GET    /api/instances/:id/graph              → { nodes:[GraphNode] }
  POST   /api/instances/:id/graph              body { prompt, agent, parent_id? |
                                                   insert_before?, mcp?, mcp_auth? }
                                                   → { node fields… }   (launches a run)
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid         body: any subset (mcp, mcp_auth,
                                                   summary, personas, active, name,
                                                   agent)
                                                   name = chain label shown in the
                                                   graph UI; empty string clears it
                                                   agent = runner for this node's
                                                   next execution (unknown agent →
                                                   400; must exist in /api/agents)
  mcp_auth is WRITE-ONLY: set/replace (non-empty string) or clear (empty
  string). It is never returned. The key is stored per machine in
  .openloop/secrets.json5 keyed by the node's mcp URL (gitignored, 0600);
  node files carry only the mcp_requires_auth marker, so the graph travels with
  the repo while keys stay local. A key without an mcp URL → 400. (No
  migration path for a plaintext mcp_auth era — it never shipped.)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid[?chain=true] → { nodes:[GraphNode] }
  POST   /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/summary body { prompt? }  → regenerate /
                                                   re-run with the edited prompt
  POST   /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/run     body { prompt, parent_run_id? }
                                                   → run log entry (prompt stored
                                                   & returned raw; context file
                                                   lines are added only at exec
                                                   time). parent_run_id = follow-up:
                                                   requires that run status
                                                   "success"; its thread's
                                                   summaries are written to
                                                   convo.md and referenced with
                                                   @/context/convo.md
  PUT    /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/runs/:rid  body { summary } → edited
                                                   run summary (enables
                                                   follow-ups on it)
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/runs/:rid → { logs:[…] } (fresh list).
                                                   Delete one run-log row:
                                                   rows whose parent_run_id
                                                   pointed at it re-parent to
                                                   its parent ("next
                                                   reparents to
                                                   deleted.parent"; nil →
                                                   they become thread roots,
                                                   root_run_id re-derived).
                                                   Deleting a parent is the
                                                   feature, not an error. The
                                                   run's notification kind
                                                   marker + read rows drop in
                                                   the same transaction.
                                                   Terminal runs only: 409
                                                   while progress/summarizing
                                                   or live in the registry,
                                                   404 wrong node anchor or
                                                   already gone.
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/runs/:rid?thread=true
                                                  → { logs:[…] } (fresh list).
                                                   The runs-list delete: the
                                                   root AND every follow-up
                                                   of its thread cascade in
                                                   one transaction (the
                                                   conversation twin of node
                                                   ?chain=true), with every
                                                   deleted row's kind marker
                                                   + read rows. Root ids
                                                   only — a follow-up :rid is
                                                   400 "Not a thread root"
                                                   (its own row has the
                                                   per-turn splice above).
                                                   409 while ANY turn of the
                                                   thread is in flight; the
                                                   node's thread-count badge
                                                   drops by one.
  GET    /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/logs    → { logs:[…] }
           Run : { id, node_id, prompt, status, output?, took?, created_at,
           completed_at?, parent_run_id?, root_run_id?, summary? }
           status: progress → summarizing → success | failed (answered =
           finished with no summary). Every successful run is summarized
           right after completion, like node creation. Summaries run
           MCP-free (no MCP_CONFIG_PATH) — MCP servers serve the answer
           phase only, everywhere.

Graph sessions — workflow follow-up conversations (the right panel of
/workflow-log.html). After a session finishes successfully, its bottom-most
persona answer can be continued like a node RUN conversation. Turns are
graph_run_logs rows anchored on the session UUID — node_id is the single
overloaded anchor column; the notification kind discriminator is a
notification_kinds marker row written in the same transaction as the insert
(absence of a marker = node run).
  GET  /api/instances/:id/graph/sessions/:sid/logs → { logs:[Run…] }
       (sid = workflow session UUID; run 0 is the seeded original answer)
  POST /api/instances/:id/graph/sessions/:sid/run   body { prompt, parent_run_id }
       → Run. Follow-up turn; re-executes the session's bottom-most persona
       (agent re-resolved from its recorded name: project bin first, then
       user local bin; unresolvable → 400). Gating mirrors node runs:
       parent must be the thread tip with a summary (409 already-continued /
       400 no-summary), thread empty → 409 seed first. Session must have a
       successful run_ends row (409 otherwise). MCP scope = the union of
       ALL the session's personas' assigned MCP servers (outer + inner
       workflows, live from the graph at turn time); ctx.md knowledge stays
       the tip persona's only.
  POST /api/instances/:id/graph/sessions/:sid/seed  → Run. Opt-in run 0:
       materializes the original answer (prompt = the session's original
       ask, output = tip persona output) and summarizes it. Empty/failed
       summarization → status "failed" (never "answered"). Duplicate → 409.
  POST /api/instances/:id/graph/sessions/:sid/runs/:rid/retry → Run.
       Failed tips only (400), no children (409), not in flight (409).
       A failed run that still holds output (seed / interrupted summary)
       retries the summarization only. Re-executed turns get the same
       union MCP scope as the run route above.
  DELETE /api/instances/:id/graph/sessions/:sid/runs/:rid → { logs:[…] }
       One turn splices out with the same semantics as the node-route DELETE
       above (follow-ups move up to the deleted run's parent; an emptied
       thread returns to the seed state). Same core, same guards — the only
       difference is the anchor: 404 when the run's row is not anchored on
       :sid.
  Manual summaries: PUT /api/instances/:id/graph/:nid/runs/:rid works for
       sessions as-is — :nid = the session UUID (no node existence check).

  GET    /api/agents                           → { agents:[{ name }] }
  Node : { id, parent_id?, prompt, agent, status, output?, took?, mcp?,
           mcp_requires_auth, mcp_auth_local, summary?, personas, active
           (dormant flag), name?, runnable,
           runs:{ total, success, failed, active }, created_at, completed_at? }
           mcp_requires_auth = the repo-traveling marker "this MCP requires
           an authorization key"; mcp_auth_local = this machine's
           secrets store holds the key for the node's URL (what runs will
           send). mcp_requires_auth && !mcp_auth_local = fresh clone: the UI asks
           the user to set the key on this computer.
           runs.active = run-log rows currently "progress" (GET /graph sweeps
           orphaned progress rows to failed first; PUT replies skip the sweep
           and heal on the next poll). total = success + failed + active.
  Node delete keeps children — they move up to the deleted node's parent, or
  become roots. ?chain=true deletes the node plus its whole subtree. Run logs
  cascade with the node(s), inside one transaction. 409 while the node (or any
  deleted node) is still running. Unlike other DELETEs this returns 200 with
  the fresh node list — never 204.

Notifications — per instance, derived from its own logs.db
(run_ends + terminal graph_run_logs, minus notification_reads markers)
  GET  /api/instances/:id/notifications?limit=100 → { items:[Notification], unread_count }
  POST /api/instances/:id/notifications/:kind/:ref/read → 200 empty body
       kind ∈ workflow (ref = session) | node_run (ref = graph_run_log id) |
              session_run (ref = graph_run_log id of a workflow follow-up)
  POST /api/instances/:id/notifications/read-all   → 200 empty body
  GET  /api/instances → each instance also carries unreadNotifications
  Notification : { id (=ref), kind, instance_path, session?, workflow_id?,
    node_id?, title, prompt?, success, took?, ended_at (unix ms), read }
  kind=workflow    → open /workflow-log.html?instance=<instance_path>&session=<session>
  kind=node_run    → open /graph.html?instance=<instance_path>&node=<node_id>&run=<run id>
                     (&run= opens that run's conversation; root_run_id maps a
                     follow-up notification to its thread root)
  kind=session_run → open /workflow-log.html?instance=<instance_path>
                     &session=<session>&run=<run id> (the follow-up thread;
                     node_id = session UUID, title = workflow name)
  Read state changes ONLY through the two POSTs above — opening a deep link
  never marks read. No poller, no separate db — everything reads logs.db live.
  Collapsing ("latest wins"): follow-up turns on one conversation and turns
  within one node Run collapse into a single notification per parent — one
  item per conversation (session) / per Run, always the latest turn's row
  (id deep-links to the newest turn; read-it-then-new-turn re-dings once).

## Core models
- Persona : { name, role, about(=system prompt), task, avatar?, agent? }
- Workflow: { name, desc, every_secs, agent, ask, levels:[[String]] }
- every_secs: -1 = run once at startup · 0 = manual only · 1 = continuous
              (next run scheduled right after finishing) · >1 = repeat every N s
- levels entries: a personaId | ":workflowId" (nested workflow) |
                  "id:rw" (force read-write).
  A level with ≥2 personas runs READ-ONLY. A single-persona level may be RO or RW.
  The last level always writes; each level sees only the previous level's output
  + the ask. Many minds analyze, then one hand acts.

## More
- Human docs (concepts, not endpoints): /docs.html
- Full trace of one run: /api/instances/:id/logs/sessions/:session
